widgets.name: Input
widgets.purpose: Single-line text entry with no chrome of its own (shadcn Input). The host supplies the surface: InputGroup when wrapped, or the tab bar for inline rename. Covers the three catalogue rows that use a bare input: inline list rename (tab bar), capture title, and sheet name (bare). The palette filter is CommandInput, the day count is NumberField, and the sheet name with fixed suffix is InputGroup with a suffix. Merged from A's TextField and B's Input. Kept A's inline size (font-medium, 140px cap, ring-1) because the weight and cap are visible. Folded the capture title's 14px/20px line into md's 21px line (1px, not felt; listed in open). Sources: A (TextField rows, text.json lines 109-116 for rename, 120-130 for commit and spellCheck, 234 for capture Tab, 311-317 for sheet) and B (Input).
widgets.base: shadcn Input (native input type=text); no Radix primitive.

values.when: Inline list rename in the tab bar. h-6 (1.5rem = 21px at 1rem=14px), px-space-4, py-0, max width 10rem (140px), font-medium (kept; B folded it to regular, see open), ring-1 on focus.

14px text on a 21px (1.5rem) line, full width of its host. Capture title, sheet name (bare). Also the md search and well fields when inside InputGroup or SearchField. The capture title's 14px/20px is folded here (see open).
12px text on an 18px line. Used inside an sm InputGroup (settings sidebar search). Inside InputGroup or SearchField the size is inherited from the owning widget; standalone the Input sets its own.

widgets.role: textbox (native input type=text; inferred from the element, not recorded in the catalogue).
widgets.keyboard: Native text editing. Enter (no Shift): onSubmit. Escape: onCancel. Blur: onBlur. Tab is not handled and bubbles (capture Tab opens notes at App.tsx:48-50). With stopKeyPropagation, every key stops at the input (inline rename). Without it, keys bubble, so a sheet's window-level Enter still accepts (catalogue line 311). Shift+Enter is not recorded for Input.
widgets.platform: Same widget on both. Capture title exists only on desktop (quick-capture window opened by global hotkey); the web has no capture window. Sheet name fields are separate windows on desktop (no backdrop dimming) and in-page dialogs on web; autoFocus and select-on-open apply in both.
widgets.open: 1) Focus indicator: use the focus ring token, not an accent border (accent reserved for primary action and selection). Decision needed; the rename uses ring-focus-1l and ring-focus-1d, the sheet uses accent-500. 2) Rename font weight: font-medium kept here, B folded it to regular. Confirm. 3) Capture title line: 14px/20px folded to md 21px (1px change, visible in principle). Confirm. 4) Keydown isolation: stopKeyPropagation default false, true only for inline rename. Confirm that capture and sheet paths bubble. 5) Select-all on open for the inline rename is inferred (catalogue rows 101-116 record no selection). 6) Sheet placeholders 'Name this list' and 'Name this project' and their aria-labels (catalogue lines 316-317) are the sheet name examples; the aria-label values were not reproduced in the critique. 7) Shift+Enter in rename, capture and sheet is not recorded.

widgets.name: InputGroup
widgets.purpose: The one chrome for text entry (shadcn InputGroup): a bordered or filled well that holds one Input plus addons. Draws the border, fill and focus ring; a press anywhere in the well focuses the Input. Two tones: field (bordered sheet well) and search (filled grey pill with no border). Merged from A's InputWell and B's InputGroup. Kept the search tone (catalogue lines 16 and 60 describe the grey pill), because the missing border is felt. Heights at 1rem=14px: md h-10 = 35px (matches the measured 345x35 sheet well); sm h-7 = 24.5px (measured 25px). The trailing slot holds the clear button and the dice roll button. Covers the sheet field well and the sheet name with a fixed suffix. Sources: A (InputWell, sheet well h-10) and B (InputGroup).
widgets.base: shadcn InputGroup (container). Its focus pattern matches the shadcn Input.

values.when: Bordered: border-edge-2 in light and dark, bg-surface-1 fill. Focus-within uses the focus ring token (see open; the sheet's accent-500 border is folded). Sheet name field and sheet well.
Filled grey rounded pill with no border. Fill and radius are not recorded in elements.json (grey in the screenshot). List search well and settings search pill.
h-7 = 1.75rem = 24.5px at 1rem=14px (measured 25px). 12px text inside. Settings sidebar search.
h-10 = 2.5rem = 35px at 1rem=14px. 14px text inside. List search well, task-list match search, sheet well and sheet name.

Decision needed (see Input open 1). 2) Search tone fill and radius are not recorded (grey only). 3) Search tone has no border, per catalogue lines 16 and 60; B's fold to sheet chrome for the search wells is rejected. Confirm. 4) The measured 35px matches h-10 at 1rem=14px; confirm the spacing scale before fixing tokens. 5) Dice roll button: which IconButton variant it uses is not in this family. 6) Suffix behaviour when the trimmed value is empty is not recorded.

widgets.name: SearchField
widgets.purpose: The one search input for the four search rows: a magnifier, a native search input, and an optional clear button, in an InputGroup search well. Covers the list search bar (filter), the task-list search (match stepping and flattening), and the settings sidebar search in plain (no clear) and with-clear forms. They share one field, placeholder and text entry, so they merge. Kept the distinctions a user feels: navigation (filter or match stepping), the clear button (clearable) and the sidebar size. Width follows its pane (layout, not a variant). Merged from A's SearchField and B's SearchField. Source: spec/catalogue/text.json. The list search bar and task-list match search are merged on identical field geometry (catalogue 14,56 832x35 well; input 46,63 733x21, as B records). This widget does not claim the trash, multi-inspector, draft-inspector or filter-panel rows (see open).
widgets.base: none (composed): InputGroup (tone search) around an Input type=search, with a leading magnifier and an optional clear IconButton from the library. No Radix primitive.

values.when: List panes: main window, multi-inspector, trash, draft-inspector, filter-panel, task-list (attribution per open). 14px/21px text, h-10 well (35px), full pane width, 18px leading icon (inferred from geometry; see open).
Settings sidebar. 12px/18px text in an h-7 well (24.5px, measured 25px). About 139px wide as measured; width follows the pane, so it is layout, not a variant. Light grey pill (tone search).
Typing filters the rows of the open list. Enter and Shift+Enter are not handled (inferred; see open).
Task list: typing filters to matching titles and flattens them. Enter steps to the next match, Shift+Enter to the previous, each focused and scrolled into view. Escape clears and blurs.

focused: focus ring token (colour is an open decision)

widgets.role: searchbox (native input type=search; inferred from the element, not recorded in the catalogue). Clear button: button with aria-label 'Clear search' (proposal; not in the reference). Leading icon is aria-hidden.
widgets.keyboard: Printable keys edit the query. filter: Enter and Shift+Enter are not handled (inferred; see open). match: Enter next, Shift+Enter previous; key events stop propagation (task list); Escape clears the query and blurs. filter with clearable (settings-general): Escape clears a non-empty query; an empty query lets Escape bubble so the host can close its window. filter with clearable false (settings-plain): Escape is not recorded (not derived from clearable; see open). Cmd/Ctrl+F: desktop focuses the field and selects its text; the web must not bind it. A typed letter from anywhere focuses the task-list field (reference behaviour; call sites partly unverified). Clear button returning focus to the input is a proposal.

Task list search, with match cycling
Settings search field, sidebar, with clear button
widgets.platform: Web: browser shortcuts take precedence, so Cmd/Ctrl+F stays browser find; the settings select-on-find is desktop only. The typed-letter focus on web is undecided (see open). Escape closing the settings window applies to the separate settings window on desktop; on web the settings view's Escape behaviour is not recorded (see open). Desktop: Cmd/Ctrl+F binds to the field; a global hotkey pressed while the main window is focused is handled by the main window.
widgets.open: 1) Focus indicator colour: the reference is a blue 1px border or outline. Accent blue is reserved for primary action and selection, so focus needs its own token unless focus counts as selection (decision needed). 2) Filter-mode Escape for the list bar and the plain settings field is not recorded. 3) Whether the task-list match search and the list search bar are the same on-screen control on the same pane is unconfirmed; merged on identical field geometry. 4) The settings search filter effect (what it filters) is unverified (catalogue lines 60 and 68). 5) Leading icon size: sm not recorded; md 18px inferred from geometry (catalogue line 17). 6) Clear button: shown only on settings-general (clearable true). B's default that added a clear button to every field is rejected; confirm. 7) Clear button aria-label 'Clear search' is a proposal. 8) Typed-letter focus from anywhere on web is undecided and may steal typing from other inputs. B's restriction (only when no editable field has focus) is a proposal, not the reference. 9) Title versus notes: row 2 description (catalogue line 40) says the task-list search filters by title and/or notes; its behaviour (line 47) says matching titles. Decide which the reference does. 10) Enter in filter mode is inferred as unhandled; the main-window onKeyDown was wired but its handler was not read. 11) Trash and multi-inspector components are recorded as '?' (catalogue line 15); draft-inspector and filter-panel attribution is unverified (lines 16 and 25-28). Assigning them to SearchField is not confirmed. 12) Settings Escape on web is a conflict between the two designs and is not recorded in the catalogue (text.json line 90, SettingsWindow.tsx:119-135). 13) Roles are inferred from the native elements, not recorded.

widgets.name: CommandInput
widgets.purpose: The filter field at the top of the command palette. It drives the palette listbox as a combobox, and its role and keys differ from a plain Input, so it is its own widget (moved out of A's TextField combobox mode). The catalogue names it a bare TextInput (text.json line 246); it is based on that. Matching is a case-insensitive substring match on the label (catalogue). Ranking by match index (earlier first, stable) is inferred from B. cmdk is an implementation option only; its default fuzzy filter must not be used unless the palette passes a substring filter.
widgets.base: Bare TextInput per the catalogue (text.json line 246) with combobox ARIA. cmdk is one implementation option, not the base.

widgets.name: TitleField
widgets.purpose: The multi-line title textarea. It grows with its content (one line 21px, two lines 42px), in a 600 18px/21px display font. Covers the task inspector title (inline) and the new-task draft title (draft). Merged from A's TitleField and B's Textarea; B's Textarea is folded in, since the same textarea and title type cover both rows and its body variant has no row. The mode axis keeps what the user feels: inline reads as text until clicked, while the draft is always editable with its own resting fill and commit or cancel rules. Radius: 4.375px (0.3125rem) recorded (catalogue lines 122 and 147), folded to the standard field radius token (open). Sources: text.json lines 109-153 (title rows) and 120-130 and 147-153 for spellCheck, commit and draft rules.
widgets.base: shadcn Textarea (native textarea, rows 1, resize none, overflow hidden, grows with content); no Radix primitive.

values.when: Task inspector title. Readonly at rest, reads as text, no fill. Click, or an editRequest from a row or F2/Enter through uiStore titleEditReq, enters editing: bg-surface-0 fill, ring-2 ring-surface-0, whole text selected on open. Enter or blur commits; Escape reverts.

New task draft title. Always editable, resting fill (about oklch(0.944 0.003 255)), ring-2 ring-surface-0, autofocus on open. Enter or blur commits the draft (runDraftAction commit); Escape cancels it (runDraftAction cancel). B folded the fill into bg-surface-0; kept here because the fill is visible (see open).

widgets.role: textbox with aria-multiline=true (native textarea; inferred from the element). readOnly sets aria-readonly.
widgets.keyboard: Enter: onCommit with the trimmed value, default prevented, so Enter never inserts a line break. Escape: onCancel, default prevented (inline reverts and exits editing; draft cancels). Blur: onCommit (trimmed). Click on a readOnly title starts editing with the text selected. F2 or Enter from a focused list row requests rename through editRequest (host). Shift+Enter is not recorded; proposal: behave as Enter with no newline.
replaces: Task title, inspector, display or edit
widgets.platform: Same widget on both. The commit on blur persists differently: web calls updateTask on the cloud API and needs a connection; desktop writes the local SQLite store. Web: commit can clash with other users' edits (multi-user; the reference is single-user). On web the draft title is the main add-task path, because there is no capture window.
widgets.open: 1) Escape on a draft with typed text: the reference cancels with an empty title; the product rule discards an untitled draft only while nothing has been added. Decide whether Escape keeps or commits typed text. 2) Blur on an empty draft runs commit with an empty title in the reference; decide whether it discards under the same rule. 3) Escape then blur ordering: Escape cancels a draft or reverts a rename (text.json lines 130 and 153) and blur commits. Proposal: a cancel suppresses the blur commit that follows. Confirm. 4) Shift+Enter in a title is not recorded (proposal above). 5) Focus ring: ring-2 ring-surface-0 is kept as recorded; decide the focus token against the accent rule (ring-focus-1l and ring-focus-1d are used by inline rename). 6) Draft resting fill kept as about oklch(0.944 0.003 255); B folded it into bg-surface-0. Decide whether the draft fill is its own token. 7) Radius 4.375px is folded to the standard field radius token; the token name is not in the catalogue. Confirm. 8) Multi-user conflict behaviour for inline commits on web is not defined by the reference. 9) Select-all on open is recorded for the task title (line 125); the draft has no selection rule.

widgets.name: RichTextEditor
widgets.purpose: The one rich-text body: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, lists, links and @mention attachments, plus drop-to-attach. Covers three rows: saved note body, add-note draft and capture notes editor. The toolbar (floating or docked) and size (sm, md, capped) keep the visible differences: toolbar placement, minimum height and capture max height. Merged from A's RichTextEditor and B's. Kept A's three sizes: the add-note draft's min-h-24 (84px) against the saved note's min-h-14 (49px) is visible, so B's fold to one md size is rejected. Font sizes are recorded as the catalogue gives them (13.5px); B's fold to 14px is listed in open. Base: common-ui/RichTextEditor.tsx:135 (catalogue lines 165, 186, 205).
widgets.base: common-ui/RichTextEditor.tsx:135 (library editor core; catalogue lines 165, 186, 205). shadcn and Radix ship no rich-text editor.

values.when: Toolbar appears on focus (opacity 100, scale 100, pointer-events auto) and hides on blur. Saved note body. The add-note draft is inferred to match (not recorded).
Toolbar always shown above the text with a top border (border-edge-1l, dark:border-edge-1d; gap-1, px-2 py-1.5). Capture notes editor. B called this 'fixed'; renamed to the catalogue's word.
Saved note body. min-h-14 = 3.5rem (49px at 1rem=14px). 13.5px text on a 17.5px (1.25rem) line.
Add-note draft. min-h-24 = 6rem (84px at 1rem=14px). Font size and line height are not recorded; the saved note's 13.5px/17.5px is an inference to confirm.
Capture notes editor. min-h-16 = 4rem (56px), max-h-40 = 10rem (140px), growing with content. 13.5px text on a 20px line.

widgets.platform: Web: Mod+B, Mod+I and Mod+U are browser shortcuts (bookmarks, view source) and browser shortcuts take precedence, so the toolbar buttons are the full path and the shortcuts a bonus (decision needed). Attachments: web uploads the dropped file to the server; desktop keeps it in local storage. Autosave: web to the cloud API, desktop to local SQLite. Capture editor is desktop-only (quick-capture window; Mod+Enter saves; Escape hides). The link dialog is a separate window on desktop. Keep the document.hasFocus() check on blur promotion on both platforms, since desktop windows can lose focus separately.
widgets.open: 1) Add-note draft toolbar mode (floating inferred) and Escape behaviour are not recorded; no Escape is inferred. 2) Font size fold: B folded 13.5px in the note and capture editors to 14px. Not applied here (recorded 13.5px); confirm. 3) Add-note min-h-24 folded to min-h-14 by B; rejected here (84px against 49px is visible). Confirm. 4) document.hasFocus() promotion on desktop: focus moving to another separate window makes the draft lose focus; decide whether that promotes the draft or keeps it open. 5) Token scale: the reference heights are 56, 96 and 64px at 16px rem; at 1rem=14px the classes resolve to 49, 84 and 56px, and max-h-40 to 140px. Confirm. 6) Focus border: the focused note body has a 2px blue border (catalogue line 167). Accent is reserved for selection and primary action, so the focus token needs a decision. 7) The mention list role and keys are not recorded. Whether Escape closes the mention list first is unknown. 8) The capture character counter is inferred. 9) The shape of the mentions source is not recorded. 10) Disabled state is not recorded in the catalogue.

widgets.name: NumberField
widgets.purpose: Narrow numeric input for the day count: centred, tabular figures, spin buttons hidden, clamped to min..max on every change. Covers the one day-count row (filter panel, shown only when the date range is custom). Kept as its own widget, not an Input type, because the clamp and centring change what the user sees and types (A's reasoning; B folded it into Input type=number, rejected here). The size axis is removed: only one size was recorded, so the compact look is fixed inside the widget (critic).
